source.title: Finding and using interpretable latents in a neutrino foundation model with sparse autoencoders
source.authors: Raphaël Bonnet-Guerrini; Johann Ioannou-Nikolaides; I. Timiryasov; Vincenzo Piuri

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. There are minor transcription/OCR errors, but they do not prevent extracting the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The study refines the claim that SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units: it reports dictionary- and layer-dependent read-outs and evidence that some information is distributed across many coordinates rather than localized in a single validated feature. It does not test toy-model superposition.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and uses the general idea of superposed representations to motivate SAEs, but it does not test feature-over-capacity, sparsity-dependent geometry, or a transition in toy networks. It studies a neutrino foundation model, not LLMs. Rows below concern the completeness and stability of SAE features; direction-head and uncertainty-head interventions are not treated as tests of canonicality because causal use by a particular head is not the same as completeness or stability of representation units.
record.test_reason: In a non-LLM transformer (PolarBERT, a neutrino model), the study measures whether SAE features hold the represented information, which it shows is often distributed, and whether they stay stable across seeds, dictionary objectives and layers. It concludes the robust object is a functional role, not a canonical latent, which bears directly on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude SAEs reveal a validated atlas of physical read-outs (quality, auxiliary activity, brightness, depth) that is not a complete inventory: it is layer-dependent, some information is distributed, and the robust object is the role rather than the latent index. They also find causal use is head-relative: the atlas is inert for the direction head but causal for an uncertainty head, which improves 20%-efficiency resolution from 20.2° to 3.2°.
record.recipe_differences: The paper applies sparse autoencoders and a validation/intervention protocol to a pretrained neutrino foundation model; it does not reproduce the toy-network setup or measurements of Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: Dictionary seed and objective, expansion and sparsity settings, and representational layer affect which read-outs are found and whether they pass validation.

fits_no_version.finding: Validated SAE read-outs are causally inert for the direction head (removal Δ ≤ 0.1°) but causal for an uncertainty head (removing z_bc gives M1 = +0.31, in 4/4 seeds). The direction head's dominant sensitivity axis matches no named feature (|cos| ≤ 0.15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether an SAE feature is causally used depends on the downstream reader, not on the feature alone.

record.problems: The study uses one neutrino foundation model and Monte Carlo data. Some physical concepts are indirect proxies; the authors note the lack of track/cascade labels. Validation and feature identification depend on dictionary and layer, and some read-outs do not pass controls across seeds.
record.rows_left_out: Not included: results on direction-head and uncertainty-head intervention effects and event-selection performance, which test head-specific causal use or downstream utility rather than whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units. Also not included: exploratory candidate rankings that fail validation and are not presented as validated read-outs.

untested.parts: No toy networks; no sparsity-dependent transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
The model is a neutrino transformer, not an LLM; spread of features across neurons is not measured.
Only one non-LLM model and BatchTopK SAEs on the CLS state are tested; the result is not shown to generalise to LLMs or other SAE architectures.
No test of whether the underlying features are one-dimensional or multi-dimensional.

missing.what: Functionally trained (e2e) dictionaries: no bright-clean analogue in the pure versions (AUROC 0.53); causal latents validate for no concept.
Clean-secondary role across seeds: passes all controls in 3/4 seeds (seed 2 fails); test AUROCs 0.679–0.744.
In seed 3 the brightness-support role is split across two latents (661, 144); the single-carrier dose response replicates in only 3/4 seeds.
Of 1024 latents, most match no tested concept, and geometry/direction candidates fail selectivity.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Toy Models only as motivation. Its setting is not an LLM, so it does not test V4. Its tranche could also be read as T3 (new setting); T5 is kept because the authors explicitly restate the unit of analysis as a functional role rather than a latent.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiment or measurement of overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
No test of capacity pressure as an explanation of polysemanticity or of important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
No test of polysemantic neurons arising without capacity pressure.
The study is about PolarBERT, a neutrino foundation model, not LLMs; it does not measure feature spread across neurons in LLMs.

Tests SAE-feature completeness and stability in one neutrino model and across specified dictionaries/layers; does not establish whether SAE features are canonical across other models, tasks, or training data.
SAE decoder vectors are directions by construction, but the study does not test whether underlying represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.
